7
Two blocks, of mass 0.20 kg and 0.50 kg, are connected by a light inextensible string that passes
over a frictionless pulley.

pulley
block,
mass 0.50 kg
The blocks are initially held stationary. The block of mass 0.20 kg rests on a rough horizontal
surface.
The block of mass 0.50 kg is suspended in air. Air resistance is negligible.
When the blocks are released, they have an acceleration of magnitude 2.0 m s–2.
What is the magnitude of the frictional force between the block of mass 0.20 kg and the rough
surface?
A
3.5 N
B
3.9 N
C
4.5 N
D
6.3 N

hints: Notice the $0.50 \text{ kg}$ hanging block pulls down with weight $m_2g$ while the string tension $T$ pulls up, giving $m_2g - T = m_2a$.
Connect the same tension $T$ to the $0.20 \text{ kg}$ block on the rough surface, where forward $T$ minus backward friction $f$ provides $m_1a$.
First calculate $T = m_2(g - a)$ with $a = 2.0 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, then use $f = T - m_1a$ to find the frictional force in $\text{N}$.
walkthrough: Identify the motion: both blocks share magnitude $a = 2.0 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ because the string is inextensible, with the $0.50 \text{ kg}$ block accelerating down and the $0.20 \text{ kg}$ block accelerating horizontally.
Apply $F = ma$ to the hanging $0.50 \text{ kg}$ block: $m_2g - T = m_2a$, so $T = m_2(g - a)$.
Substitute with units, using $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$: $T = 0.50 \times (9.81 - 2.0) = 0.50 \times 7.81 = 3.905 \text{ N}$.
Apply $F = ma$ to the $0.20 \text{ kg}$ block: $T - f = m_1a$, so $f = T - m_1a$.

A.explanation: Friction is $T - m_1a = 3.9 - 0.40 = 3.5 \text{ N}$ for the $0.20 \text{ kg}$ block.

B.explanation: This is the string tension $T = 3.9 \text{ N}$ acting on the $0.50 \text{ kg}$ block, before subtracting $m_1a$ for friction.

C.explanation: This uses $T - f = 0$ with no acceleration for the $0.20 \text{ kg}$ block, ignoring the $0.40 \text{ N}$ resultant force needed.

D.explanation: This adds friction and tension incorrectly, close to $m_2g + m_1a$ rather than using $T - f = m_1a$.
